elements.quote: Although the issue of growing prevalence of obesity among women of reproductive age has been previously addressed in many LMICs, such as Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and India, the problem has been underestimated in Pakistan because of scarcity of relevant data and lack of focussed policy in place. To date, fewer studies in published literature have focussed on examining in depth the socio-demographic, environmental, lifestyle and dietary patterns and other factors contributing to nutrition transition in Pakistan mainly in the women of reproductive years.
elements.reason: The text describes the current state of knowledge (obesity in LMICs) and the uncertainty/gap in Pakistan regarding the specific determinants of obesity in women of reproductive age.

elements.quote: This review article was planned to highlight the nutrition transition in Pakistan by exploring the factors contributing to rise in overweight and obesity among women of reproductive age (15-49 years), and possible policy recommendation for policy-makers to deal with this challenge.

elements.quote: In contrast, a review of literature from developed countries showed a strong inverse relationship between SES and obesity among women living in developed societies. 14 There is also evidence from literature that women living in high SES societies in developed countries have greater access to healthier food and greater proportion of fruits in their diet. 15 However, studies in LICs show that higher SES is a contributing factor towards obesity presumably because of moremoneyspentonfood, use of better transport for commuting, sedentary living behaviours etc. 16 Moreover, studies also showed a recent shift in obesity towards groups of LES in LICs as their gross defendant product (GDP) rises. 17 This is consistent with our finding of growing trend of obesity and overweight among females living in households with LES.
elements.reason: The authors interpret their findings regarding the relationship between socioeconomic status (SES) and obesity in Pakistan by comparing them with existing literature from both developed countries and other low-income countries (LICs).
